## Packages


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(palmerpenguins)
library(tidyverse)
```
:::


## Motivating Question 

I want you to compare the mean flipper length between Adelie penguins and Gentoo penguins from the palmerpenguins package. Specifically, I want to investigate if the mean flipper length is different between these two species.

## EDA


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
peng_sub <- penguins |> 
  filter(species %in% c("Adelie", "Gentoo"))

peng_sub |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(mean_fl = mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = T),
            sd_fl = sd(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = T))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 2 x 3
  species mean_fl sd_fl
  <fct>     <dbl> <dbl>
1 Adelie     190.  6.54
2 Gentoo     217.  6.48
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
peng_sub |>
  ggplot(
    aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm)
  ) + 
  geom_boxplot()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}

```

(`stat_boxplot()`).
```

But we can't claim that the population mean flipper length of Gentoo penguins is larger than Adelie because sampling variability is thing. 

## Hypothesis Test 

$H_o: \mu_a - \mu_g = 0$

$H_a: \mu_a - \mu_g \neq 0$

$\bar{x}_a - \bar{x}_g = -27$


## Check our assumptions 

-- independence 

Comes down to how we sample! Collect data through a simple random sample.

-- normality 

Check our sample size! Are the counts $n \ge$ 30.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
peng_sub |>
  group_by(species) |>
  count()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
# A tibble: 2 x 2
# Groups:   species [2]
  species     n
  <fct>   <int>
1 Adelie    152
2 Gentoo    124
```


:::
:::

## t-test


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
t.test(flipper_length_mm ~ species,
       data = peng_sub,
       var.equal = TRUE) # this argument looks at our equal variance assumption!
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```

	Two Sample t-test

data:  flipper_length_mm by species
t = -34.415, df = 272, p-value < 2.2e-16
alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Adelie and group Gentoo is not equal to 0
95 percent confidence interval:
 -28.79125 -25.67545
sample estimates:
mean in group Adelie mean in group Gentoo 
            189.9536             217.1870 
```


:::
:::



Assume $\alpha$ is 0.05!

P-value < $\alpha$ = Reject the null hypothesis

P-value = Probability of observing -27 (t = -34.445), or something "more extreme" given the population mean flipper length for Adelie penguins is the same as Gentoo penguins is < 2.2e-16.
